p5_execution_focus: Run the renewal pipeline live, route selected renewals into competitive sourcing or renegotiation, and track captured savings in a regular cadence.
tower_metrics: Percent of renewals reviewed before their notice deadline; Number and value of contracts that auto-renewed unmanaged; Savings captured from renegotiated or re-sourced renewals; Renewal pipeline value visible 6-12 months out; Share of high-value renewals actively managed
required_controls: Human decision required before any renewal or non-renewal action; Clear ownership of each renewal decision; Audit trail of recommendations and actions taken; Data-quality checks flagging missing or uncertain renewal dates; Confidentiality of contract commercial terms
client_stakeholders: Corporate VP of Procurement / Shared Services; Category managers; Operating-company procurement and finance leads; Legal (for notice-period and termination terms); Corporate finance / FP&A (for savings validation)
what_good_looks_like: A single forward view of every renewal across operating companies, ranked by value and leverage, with clear recommended actions, so procurement acts before deadlines instead of discovering auto-renewals after the fact.
biggest_risks_traps: Incomplete or wrong renewal dates make the pipeline untrustworthy and cause missed deadlines; Recommended actions may misjudge leverage without real market or usage context; Savings claims may be double-counted or unverified without finance sign-off; Operating companies may not surface all their contracts into the shared view
gaps_in_current_moves_model: Heavy dependence on data readiness that the Moves model treats as a prerequisite but doesn't scope well as part of the same move; Savings-attribution logic between this move, Source, and Tower is not clearly defined to avoid double-counting; No standard pattern for confidence-scoring renewal dates so leads know which to trust

business_outcome: Corporate shared services get an evidence-based view of how key suppliers perform across operating companies, so Lakeshore can hold suppliers accountable, focus improvement on the worst performers, and use consolidated leverage in negotiations.
current_state_work_problem: Supplier performance is judged anecdotally and separately by each operating company. The same supplier may be praised in one and criticized in another with no shared record. Delivery, quality, and service data sit in different systems, so there is no consistent scorecard and no consolidated view to drive supplier reviews or negotiations.
phase_one_solution_approach: Build a supplier performance intelligence layer that pulls available delivery, quality, spend, and issue data into a consistent scorecard per supplier, consolidated across operating companies. A procurement lead reviews and interprets the scorecard for business reviews; the tool surfaces insights but doesn't score suppliers as final fact or trigger actions. Feeds Tower for value and negotiation leverage.
building_blocks: Data readiness/remediation; Analytics/intelligence layer; AI-assisted decision support; Human-in-the-loop agent; Value tracking/operating cadence
building_blocks_not_yet: Workflow automation: Automated supplier actions (holds, penalties, escalations) require trusted, complete data and clear policy; unsafe until scorecards are validated.; Controls/governance/risk: Formal supplier-consequence governance is a later layer; phase one is about visibility, not enforcement.; Knowledge/retrieval copilot: A supplier-review copilot is useful later but depends on a trusted scorecard foundation first.
required_p2_evidence: Available delivery, quality, and service data per supplier across operating companies; Current spend by supplier consolidated across the group; Examples of how supplier reviews are run today and what data they use; Known data gaps and inconsistencies across operating-company systems; Which suppliers are strategic / highest-spend and shared across operating companies
p2_current_state_focus: Understand what performance data actually exists, how reliable it is, and how supplier reviews are conducted today across operating companies.
p3_solution_approach_focus: Design the consistent supplier scorecard, the consolidated cross-operating-company view, and how a lead interprets insights in reviews.
p4_roadmap_value_focus: Justify the move on better negotiation leverage, focused supplier improvement, and consolidated spend visibility; start with strategic, shared suppliers.
p5_execution_focus: Use scorecards live in supplier business reviews, track performance improvement and negotiation outcomes, and refine data sources in a regular cadence.
tower_metrics: Share of strategic suppliers with a consistent scorecard; Performance improvement in worst-performing suppliers over time; Consolidated spend visibility across operating companies; Negotiation savings enabled by performance evidence; Number of supplier reviews run on shared data
required_controls: Human interpretation required before performance conclusions are shared with suppliers; Clear labeling of data confidence and gaps on each scorecard; Audit trail of data sources feeding each score; Fair-treatment guardrails so incomplete data doesn't unfairly penalize a supplier; Confidentiality of supplier-specific performance data
client_stakeholders: Corporate VP of Procurement / Shared Services; Category and supplier relationship managers; Operating-company operations and quality leads; Finance (for consolidated spend); Strategic suppliers (as review participants)
what_good_looks_like: One consistent, evidence-based scorecard per strategic supplier consolidated across operating companies, clearly showing data confidence, used to run sharper supplier reviews and negotiate from consolidated leverage.
biggest_risks_traps: Data is patchy and inconsistent across operating companies, undermining scorecard credibility; Comparing suppliers on unequal data can be unfair and damage relationships; Leads may treat AI-surfaced scores as objective truth rather than a starting point; Operating companies may resist a central view of their supplier relationships
gaps_in_current_moves_model: Moves model underestimates the data-remediation effort needed before a credible scorecard exists; No standard way to show and act on data-confidence levels so weak data isn't over-trusted; Fair-comparison guardrails for suppliers with uneven data are not part of the model

business_outcome: Lakeshore's corporate shared services get visibility and light-touch control over the long tail of low-value, fragmented purchases across operating companies, so off-contract 'maverick' buying is reduced, spend is steered to preferred suppliers, and savings are captured on spend that today gets no procurement attention.
current_state_work_problem: A large share of purchases are small, one-off, and made outside preferred contracts by many buyers across operating companies. Nobody has time to manage this tail, so the group pays more than it should, uses too many suppliers for the same category, and can't see where off-contract buying is happening or why.
phase_one_solution_approach: Build an analytics layer that classifies and consolidates tail spend across operating companies, surfaces where buying goes off preferred contracts, and recommends where to steer purchases or consolidate suppliers. A procurement analyst reviews the patterns and decides on interventions (guidance, catalog changes, supplier consolidation); the tool recommends and does not block or redirect purchases automatically. Consolidation candidates feed AbarVa's Source surface and savings feed Tower.
building_blocks: Data readiness/remediation; Analytics/intelligence layer; AI-assisted decision support; Process redesign; Value tracking/operating cadence
building_blocks_not_yet: Workflow automation: Automatically blocking or redirecting purchases risks disrupting operations; phase one steers behavior through guidance and catalogs, not hard automation.; Human-in-the-loop agent: A per-transaction review agent isn't warranted at tail-spend volumes yet; phase one works at the pattern level, not transaction by transaction.; Controls/governance/risk: Formal purchasing-policy enforcement is a later step once patterns and preferred-supplier guidance are established.
required_p2_evidence: Full spend data across operating companies with supplier and category detail; Definition of preferred contracts and catalogs today; Estimate of spend going off-contract and to fragmented suppliers; Buyer population and how tail purchases are made today; Data-quality assessment of spend categorization
p2_current_state_focus: Quantify the size and shape of tail spend, how much is off-contract, and where fragmentation and price leakage are worst.
p3_solution_approach_focus: Design the spend classification, the off-contract detection, the recommended interventions, and how analysts act on them without disrupting operations.
p4_roadmap_value_focus: Size savings from consolidation and on-contract steering; prioritize the categories with the most fragmented, highest-leakage tail spend.
p5_execution_focus: Run tail-spend interventions live (catalog updates, supplier consolidation, buyer guidance), track on-contract rate and savings, and review in a regular cadence.
tower_metrics: Percent of spend on preferred contracts (on-contract rate); Reduction in supplier count for consolidated categories; Savings captured from tail-spend consolidation; Share of tail spend with clear category visibility; Off-contract spend trend across operating companies
required_controls: Human decision on every intervention before it affects buyers; Clear labeling of spend-classification confidence; Audit trail of recommended and implemented interventions; Guardrails so steering doesn't disrupt urgent or operational purchases; Confidentiality of operating-company spend detail
client_stakeholders: Corporate VP of Procurement / Shared Services; Category managers; Operating-company finance and operations leads; Accounts payable / P2P owners; Corporate finance / FP&A (for savings validation)
what_good_looks_like: Shared services can see the whole tail of spend across operating companies, know where off-contract buying happens, and steer purchases to preferred suppliers with clear savings, turning previously ignored spend into managed savings.
biggest_risks_traps: Poor spend classification produces misleading tail-spend numbers; Over-aggressive steering frustrates buyers and pushes them further off-system; Savings estimates may be optimistic without finance validation and a baseline; Operating-company autonomy makes central steering politically hard
gaps_in_current_moves_model: Spend-classification data readiness is a large hidden effort the Moves model doesn't scope cleanly within the move; No standard baseline-and-attribution method to make tail-spend savings claims defensible to finance; Change-management for buyer behavior across autonomous operating companies is under-modeled

business_outcome: Employee and manager questions and issues reaching the shared-services HR team are understood, prioritized, and routed to the right specialist or operating-company HR partner on first touch, cutting time-to-first-response and reducing cases that bounce between teams.
current_state_work_problem: HR shared services at Lakeshore receives a mixed inbound stream (email, portal tickets, phone follow-ups) spanning payroll, benefits, leave, workplace concerns, and manager queries across several operating companies. Cases are manually read, categorized, and assigned by a small intake team. Categories are inconsistent, urgent or sensitive matters (harassment, ADA, whistleblower) are sometimes missed in the queue, and cross-operating-company cases get misrouted, driving rework and slow response.
phase_one_solution_approach: A human-in-the-loop triage assistant that reads each incoming case, proposes a category, urgency, sensitivity flag, and suggested owner/operating company, and drafts a first-response acknowledgement. An intake specialist confirms or corrects every routing decision before it takes effect. Sensitive categories are always escalated to a named human, never auto-closed. No adverse or eligibility decision is ever made by the assistant.
building_blocks: Process redesign; Knowledge/retrieval copilot; AI-assisted decision support; Human-in-the-loop agent; Controls/governance/risk; Value tracking/operating cadence
building_blocks_not_yet: Workflow automation: Auto-routing without a human confirming the owner is unsafe while category accuracy is unproven and sensitive-case handling must stay with people; automate only after triage accuracy is measured over a pilot.; System/platform implementation: Phase one should sit on top of the existing HR case tool rather than replacing it; a platform change is a later decision once the triage model earns trust.
required_p2_evidence: A representative sample of past cases with their true category, urgency, and correct owner, agreed with HR intake leads; The current category and routing rules used across operating companies, and where they conflict; Definitions of sensitive case types (harassment, ADA/accommodation, whistleblower, investigations) and their mandated handling paths; Baseline metrics: current time-to-first-response, misroute rate, and reopen/bounce rate; Data privacy and retention rules for HR case content, including who may see what across operating companies
p2_current_state_focus: Map how cases actually flow today across operating companies, quantify misroutes and response delays, and document where sensitive matters must bypass any automation. Confirm what employee data the intake process legitimately touches.
p3_solution_approach_focus: Design the triage taxonomy, the confidence thresholds at which the assistant may suggest versus must defer, the mandatory human-review points, and the sensitive-case escalation path. Define what a good acknowledgement draft looks like and the specialist's confirm/correct interaction.
p4_roadmap_value_focus: Size the value from faster first response and fewer misroutes, phase the rollout operating-company by operating-company, and build the business case against current intake effort and reopen cost.
p5_execution_focus: Run the assistant in suggest-only mode with specialists confirming every routing, track accuracy and correction rate weekly, and expand categories only as accuracy holds.
tower_metrics: Time-to-first-response; First-touch correct-routing rate; Case reopen / bounce rate; Sensitive-case escalation compliance rate; Cases handled per intake specialist
required_controls: Every routing decision confirmed by a human before it takes effect during pilot; Sensitive categories always escalated to a named person and never auto-closed; Access to case content scoped by operating company and role; Full audit trail of suggested versus final routing for every case; No eligibility, disciplinary, or adverse decision made by the assistant
client_stakeholders: VP HR Shared Services; HR Intake / Service Center lead; Operating-company HR business partners; Employee Relations / Investigations lead; HR Data Privacy / Compliance; Works council / employee representatives where applicable
what_good_looks_like: Cases are correctly categorized and routed on first touch the large majority of the time, sensitive matters reach the right specialist immediately, first-response time drops materially, and intake specialists spend their time resolving rather than sorting — with a clear audit trail behind every routing decision.
biggest_risks_traps: A sensitive case (harassment, ADA, whistleblower) mis-categorized as routine and buried in a general queue; Employee case content crossing operating-company boundaries it should not; Specialists rubber-stamping suggestions once volume rises, eroding the human-in-the-loop safeguard; Taxonomy that looks clean in design but does not match how employees actually phrase issues; Perception among employees that a machine is judging their HR issue
gaps_in_current_moves_model: No built-in notion of a 'sensitive item must bypass automation' rule as a first-class control on a building block; Value tracking assumes clean baselines; HR intake baselines are often not instrumented before the Move starts; The model does not yet express confidence-threshold gating (suggest vs. defer) as a designable parameter

business_outcome: Managers across Lakeshore's operating companies get consistent, compliant, market-aligned job descriptions produced in hours rather than weeks, with a clean approval trail — speeding hiring and reducing inconsistency and legal exposure in postings.
current_state_work_problem: Each operating company writes job descriptions its own way. Managers copy old postings, language drifts, pay-transparency and equal-opportunity requirements are applied inconsistently, and levels/titles don't map to any shared framework. HR compliance reviews are manual, slow, and easy to skip, so postings go out with inconsistent or non-compliant language.
phase_one_solution_approach: A drafting assistant that generates a first job-description draft from a manager's inputs (role, level, must-haves) grounded in Lakeshore's approved templates, job-level framework, and required legal language. The manager edits, then it routes through a defined HR/compliance approval before publishing. The assistant drafts; humans own every approval. It flags missing pay-transparency or EEO language rather than silently inserting decisions.
building_blocks: Process redesign; Knowledge/retrieval copilot; Workflow automation; Human-in-the-loop agent; Controls/governance/risk
building_blocks_not_yet: Data readiness/remediation: A clean shared job-level and title framework may not exist yet across operating companies; if it's missing, that becomes its own upstream effort rather than something to assume in phase one.; Analytics/intelligence layer: Market-benchmark and pay-equity analytics on postings are valuable but a later layer once consistent, well-structured descriptions exist to analyze.; Value tracking/operating cadence: Worth adding once volume is real; early on the win is qualitative consistency and speed, measurable but not yet a standing cadence.
required_p2_evidence: Lakeshore's approved job-description templates and any shared job-level / title framework; Required legal language by jurisdiction (pay transparency, EEO, accommodation statements); A sample of recent postings showing current inconsistency and compliance gaps; The real approval chain for postings in each operating company; Baseline time-to-post and rework/return rate on descriptions
p2_current_state_focus: Document how descriptions are actually created and approved today, where compliant language is missing, and whether a usable shared level/title framework exists or must be built.
p3_solution_approach_focus: Design the input form managers fill, the grounding sources the draft must use, the compliance checks the assistant must surface, and the approval routing and sign-off record.
p4_roadmap_value_focus: Quantify time saved and compliance-risk reduction, sequence rollout by operating company and job family, and decide whether a shared level framework is a prerequisite workstream.
p5_execution_focus: Publish only through the approval workflow, monitor edit-distance and rejection reasons to improve drafts, and track adoption by managers.
tower_metrics: Time-to-post (request to approved description); Compliance-language completeness rate; Approval rework / return rate; Manager adoption rate; Consistency score against the shared framework
required_controls: No description published without the defined HR/compliance approval; Required legal language flagged and confirmed present, never silently auto-inserted as a decision; Jurisdiction-specific requirements applied based on posting location; Full record of who approved each description and when; Templates and legal language are versioned and centrally owned
client_stakeholders: VP HR Shared Services; Talent Acquisition lead; Compensation / Job Architecture lead; HR Compliance / Employment Counsel; Operating-company hiring managers; DEI lead
what_good_looks_like: A manager describes a role in minutes, gets a clean draft grounded in Lakeshore's framework with the right legal language already flagged, edits lightly, and it moves through approval and to posting fast — with descriptions looking consistent across operating companies and audit-ready.
biggest_risks_traps: Missing or wrong jurisdiction-specific pay-transparency or EEO language creating legal exposure; Bias or non-inclusive language slipping into drafts and being copied at scale; No shared level framework, so 'consistency' has nothing to anchor to; Managers bypassing the tool and posting old descriptions anyway; Approval step treated as a formality and skipped under hiring pressure
gaps_in_current_moves_model: The model treats a prerequisite like 'shared job-level framework exists' as an assumption rather than surfacing it as a gating dependency at P2; No first-class way to express jurisdiction-conditional required content as a control; Bias/inclusive-language review isn't represented as a distinct check the design must include

business_outcome: Employees and managers get fast, accurate, source-cited answers to HR policy questions (leave, benefits, expenses, conduct) tailored to their operating company and location, deflecting routine questions from the HR service center and reducing inconsistent guidance.
current_state_work_problem: Policies differ by operating company and jurisdiction, live in scattered handbooks and intranet pages, and are often outdated. Employees can't tell which version applies to them, so they email HR or ask managers, who sometimes guess. The HR service center is flooded with repetitive policy questions, and inconsistent answers create fairness and compliance risk.
phase_one_solution_approach: A retrieval copilot that answers policy questions only from Lakeshore's current, approved policy documents, always shows the source and effective date, and scopes answers to the employee's operating company and location. When policy is unclear, conflicting, or the question touches an individual's situation (leave eligibility, discipline, accommodation), it hands off to a human rather than answering. It informs; it does not decide entitlements.
building_blocks: Data readiness/remediation; Knowledge/retrieval copilot; Human-in-the-loop agent; Controls/governance/risk; Value tracking/operating cadence
building_blocks_not_yet: AI-assisted decision support: Determining an individual's eligibility or entitlement is a decision that must stay with HR; phase one answers general policy only and hands individual cases to people.; Workflow automation: Triggering downstream actions (e.g., filing a leave request) from an answer is premature until answer accuracy and hand-off boundaries are proven.
required_p2_evidence: The authoritative, current set of policies per operating company and jurisdiction, with owners and effective dates; A list of known outdated, duplicate, or conflicting policy documents to remediate; The most common policy questions and today's answer sources; Clear boundaries of what counts as general policy vs. an individual entitlement decision; Baseline volume of policy questions hitting the service center and current answer accuracy/consistency
p2_current_state_focus: Establish which policy documents are truly authoritative and current, find the conflicts and stale versions, and define the line between answerable general policy and questions that must go to a human.
p3_solution_approach_focus: Design source-grounding and mandatory citation, operating-company/jurisdiction scoping, the confidence and topic rules that trigger human hand-off, and the phrasing that avoids sounding like an entitlement decision.
p4_roadmap_value_focus: Size deflection of routine questions and consistency gains, and scope the policy-cleanup effort as an explicit prerequisite investment.
p5_execution_focus: Launch on a limited, well-governed policy set, monitor answer accuracy and hand-off rate, feed unanswered/incorrect questions back into policy remediation, and expand coverage as content is cleaned.
tower_metrics: Policy-question deflection rate from the service center; Answer accuracy (human-audited sample); Correct hand-off rate on out-of-scope/individual questions; Source-citation and currency rate; Employee satisfaction with answers
required_controls: Answers only from approved, current policy sources — no free-form generation of policy; Every answer shows its source and effective date; Answers scoped to the employee's operating company and jurisdiction; Individual-situation and unclear questions handed to a human, never answered as entitlement; Stale/conflicting content quarantined until remediated
client_stakeholders: VP HR Shared Services; HR Policy / Total Rewards owners; HR Service Center lead; Employment Counsel / Compliance; Operating-company HR partners; Internal Communications / intranet owner
what_good_looks_like: An employee asks a policy question, gets a clear answer scoped to their operating company with the exact source and effective date, and trusts it — while anything touching their individual entitlement is smoothly handed to HR. Routine question volume to the service center drops and answers are consistent everywhere.
biggest_risks_traps: Answering from an outdated or wrong-jurisdiction policy and giving employees false assurance; Drifting from 'here's the policy' into 'here's your entitlement,' which is a decision HR must own; Content debt: without policy cleanup, the copilot confidently cites contradictory documents; Employees treating the answer as binding when it should point to HR for their case; Coverage gaps read as authoritative silence
gaps_in_current_moves_model: The heavy upstream policy-remediation dependency is easy to under-scope; the model doesn't force sizing it before promising deflection; No first-class 'answer vs. decide' boundary control that this use case critically needs; Currency/effective-date of source content isn't represented as a tracked quality gate

business_outcome: New hires across Lakeshore's operating companies are productive on day one because every onboarding task — accounts, access, equipment, payroll setup, compliance training, manager check-ins — is triggered, tracked, and completed on time, with nothing dropped between HR, IT, facilities, and the operating company.
current_state_work_problem: Onboarding spans HR, IT, facilities, payroll, and the hiring operating company, coordinated by checklists and email. Tasks fall through the cracks, new hires arrive without laptops or system access, compliance training lapses go unnoticed, and no one has a single view of onboarding status. It varies widely by operating company and depends on individual coordinators remembering steps.
phase_one_solution_approach: A workflow that generates the right onboarding task list for each new hire based on role, operating company, and location, assigns tasks to the correct owners, tracks completion, and surfaces a live status view with reminders and escalations for anything overdue. Humans still perform the tasks and sign off on compliance-critical steps; the orchestration coordinates and chases rather than granting access or clearing requirements itself.
building_blocks: Process redesign; Workflow automation; Human-in-the-loop agent; Analytics/intelligence layer; Controls/governance/risk; Value tracking/operating cadence
building_blocks_not_yet: System/platform implementation: Phase one should orchestrate across existing HR, IT, and payroll systems rather than deploy a new onboarding platform; consolidation is a later decision once the flow is proven.; AI-assisted decision support: Access provisioning and compliance clearance are governed decisions that must stay with their owners; the assistant coordinates, it does not grant access or waive requirements.
required_p2_evidence: The full onboarding task set by role, operating company, and location, and who owns each task; Which systems must be touched (identity/access, payroll, learning, equipment) and how status can be read from them; Compliance-critical steps that legally must be completed before start or within a window; Baseline: on-time completion rate, day-one readiness rate, and where tasks currently drop; Access-governance rules — separation of duties, approvals required before provisioning
p2_current_state_focus: Map the real end-to-end onboarding flow across all owners and systems, quantify where and how often it breaks, and pin down the compliance-critical steps that cannot be missed.
p3_solution_approach_focus: Design role/company-specific task generation, ownership and assignment rules, the reminder/escalation logic, the live status view, and which steps require human sign-off before the hire proceeds.
p4_roadmap_value_focus: Quantify day-one readiness gains and coordinator time saved, and sequence rollout by operating company and role type.
p5_execution_focus: Run the orchestration live with owners still executing tasks, track on-time completion and day-one readiness weekly, and tune task templates from misses and escalations.
tower_metrics: Day-one readiness rate (all critical tasks complete at start); On-time task completion rate; Compliance-training completion within required window; Onboarding coordinator hours per hire; New-hire onboarding experience score
required_controls: Access and account provisioning still executed and approved by their governed owners, not by the orchestrator; Compliance-critical steps explicitly signed off before a hire is marked ready; Separation-of-duties and approval rules preserved for provisioning; Full audit trail of task status, owners, and sign-offs per hire; New-hire personal data scoped to the operating company and roles that need it
client_stakeholders: VP HR Shared Services; Onboarding / HR Operations lead; IT identity & access management lead; Payroll lead; Facilities / equipment lead; Operating-company hiring managers; Compliance / Learning lead
what_good_looks_like: Every new hire's tasks are generated automatically for their role and operating company, each owner knows exactly what to do and by when, overdue items escalate before they become day-one failures, and HR has one live view of readiness — with access and compliance steps still owned and signed off by the right people.
biggest_risks_traps: Treating orchestration as authority to grant access, breaking access-governance and separation of duties; A compliance-critical step (e.g., mandated safety or background check) marked done without real sign-off; Status that looks green because a system integration is stale, not because work is actually done; Task templates that don't reflect real operating-company differences, so the list is wrong; New-hire personal data over-shared across owners and operating companies
gaps_in_current_moves_model: The model doesn't cleanly separate 'coordinate a task' from 'have authority to complete it,' which is the core safety line here; Status accuracy depends on reading other systems' state, and integration-freshness isn't a tracked quality gate in the model; Compliance-critical sign-off as a hard gate isn't a first-class control concept

use_case: Leave and accommodation intake and status assistant
business_outcome: Employees requesting leave (FMLA, medical, parental) or a workplace accommodation get a clear, guided intake and reliable status updates, while the sensitive eligibility and accommodation decisions stay firmly with HR specialists — reducing errors, delays, and compliance risk across operating companies.
current_state_work_problem: Leave and accommodation requests are among the most sensitive and legally exposed HR processes, and at Lakeshore they vary by operating company and jurisdiction. Employees don't know what to submit, requests stall waiting on missing documentation, status is opaque so employees repeatedly chase HR, and inconsistent handling across operating companies creates real FMLA/ADA compliance and fairness risk.
phase_one_solution_approach: An assistant that guides the employee through what a given leave or accommodation request needs, checks that required documentation is present, explains general process and timelines with sources, and gives status updates — while every eligibility and accommodation decision, and all medical information, is handled by an HR specialist. It collects and informs; it never determines eligibility, approves leave, or interprets medical information. Sensitive health data is tightly restricted.
building_blocks: Process redesign; Knowledge/retrieval copilot; Workflow automation; Human-in-the-loop agent; Controls/governance/risk; Value tracking/operating cadence
building_blocks_not_yet: AI-assisted decision support: Leave eligibility and accommodation determinations are legally sensitive, individualized decisions that must stay entirely with HR specialists and counsel — the assistant must not suggest outcomes.; Analytics/intelligence layer: Aggregate leave/accommodation analytics are valuable for capacity and equity but must wait until data handling and privacy controls are proven and access is tightly scoped.; System/platform implementation: Phase one guides intake and status on top of existing leave administration; replacing the system of record for a legally exposed process is a later, deliberate decision.
required_p2_evidence: Leave and accommodation types and their legal requirements by jurisdiction (FMLA, ADA, state leave, parental); Required documentation and timelines per request type; The strict boundary between guidance/intake and any eligibility or medical determination; How and where sensitive medical information is stored and who may access it; Baseline: request cycle time, documentation-completeness rate, and status-chasing volume to HR
p2_current_state_focus: Map each leave/accommodation type's legal requirements and current handling across operating companies, and rigorously define what the assistant may touch versus what must stay with specialists and counsel — especially around medical information.
p3_solution_approach_focus: Design the guided intake, documentation checks, source-cited general-process answers, secure hand-off to specialists, and status updates — with hard walls around eligibility decisions and medical data.
p4_roadmap_value_focus: Size faster, more complete intake and reduced status-chasing, and scope the strict privacy and access controls as non-negotiable prerequisites.
p5_execution_focus: Pilot in one operating company with specialists owning all decisions, monitor documentation-completeness and cycle time, and confirm zero decisioning or medical-data leakage before expanding.
tower_metrics: Request cycle time (submission to decision); Documentation-completeness rate at first submission; Reduction in employee status-chasing contacts; On-time compliance with statutory leave timelines; Employee experience score for the leave/accommodation process
required_controls: Assistant never determines eligibility, approves leave, or interprets medical information; Sensitive medical data segregated with strict, minimal, audited access; Jurisdiction-specific legal requirements enforced and surfaced to specialists; Every request handed to a named HR specialist for decision, with full audit trail; Employee data scoped to the operating company and specialists handling the case
client_stakeholders: VP HR Shared Services; Leave & Accommodation / Benefits specialists; Employment Counsel / Compliance; HR Data Privacy officer; Operating-company HR partners; Occupational health / medical data custodian
what_good_looks_like: An employee is guided to submit a complete leave or accommodation request the first time, always knows where it stands, and reaches a specialist quickly — while every eligibility and accommodation decision and all medical information stay with trained HR people under strict privacy controls, consistently across operating companies.
biggest_risks_traps: The assistant drifting into implying an eligibility outcome — a serious legal and fairness breach; Any mishandling or over-exposure of sensitive medical/health information; Inconsistent jurisdiction handling creating FMLA/ADA compliance violations; Employees perceiving automation in a deeply personal process as cold or dismissive; Guidance mistaken for a decision, creating false expectations and disputes
gaps_in_current_moves_model: The model has no first-class concept of a hard 'never decide / never interpret medical data' wall that this use case absolutely requires; Handling of specially protected data categories (medical/health) isn't represented as a distinct control tier; Phase-one realism suffers because the model doesn't force the privacy/legal prerequisites to be sized before the Move is greenlit

business_outcome: Cut the time and effort corporate shared services spends running periodic access reviews across operating-company systems, while raising the quality and auditability of every recertification decision so entitlements that should be revoked actually get revoked on time.
current_state_work_problem: Every quarter, corporate IT security pulls entitlement extracts from dozens of systems across Lakeshore's operating companies, formats them into spreadsheets, and emails them to hundreds of manager-reviewers. Reviewers rubber-stamp long lists they don't understand, context on what each entitlement grants is missing, revocations get lost in email threads, and the audit team spends weeks chasing incomplete campaigns and reassembling proof that reviews actually happened.
phase_one_solution_approach: A reviewer-facing copilot that assembles each manager's recertification packet with plain-language context (what the access grants, when it was last used, peer comparison, risk flags) and recommends keep/revoke, while the human reviewer makes and signs every decision. Revocation requests are routed to system owners; the campaign's completeness and every decision are captured as tamper-evident audit evidence.
building_blocks: Knowledge/retrieval copilot; AI-assisted decision support; Human-in-the-loop agent; Controls/governance/risk; Value tracking/operating cadence
building_blocks_not_yet: Workflow automation: Auto-executing revocations against production systems is too risky at P1; certification decisions must stay human-signed and revocation execution stays a controlled, owner-approved step until trust and rollback are proven.; System/platform implementation: Replacing or standing up a new identity-governance platform is a multi-quarter program; P1 rides on top of existing entitlement extracts rather than re-platforming.; Data readiness/remediation: Some entitlement remediation is needed, but the first move focuses on decision quality; deep source-data cleanup is scoped as a follow-on once gaps are quantified.
required_p2_evidence: Current recertification campaign calendar, scope, and populations by operating company; Sample entitlement extracts from the top 5-10 in-scope systems; Last two campaigns' completion rates, cycle time, and overdue/exception counts; Audit and internal-control findings from prior access-review cycles; List of privileged/high-risk entitlement types and current owners/approvers
p2_current_state_focus: Map how recertification runs today end to end, quantify reviewer burden and rubber-stamp rate, and expose where revocations fall through and where audit evidence is thin or missing.
p3_solution_approach_focus: Design the reviewer packet, the recommendation logic and its risk flags, the human sign-off and revocation-routing flow, and the evidence trail — being explicit that recommendations are advisory and every decision is human-owned.
p4_roadmap_value_focus: Quantify reviewer hours saved, cycle-time reduction, and reduction in overdue/stale access; phase rollout system-by-system starting with highest-risk populations; build the business case on audit-readiness and reduced access risk.
p5_execution_focus: Run live campaigns on a recurring cadence, track completion and revocation follow-through, monitor recommendation quality against reviewer overrides, and report audit-readiness to the control owners each cycle.
tower_metrics: Recertification cycle time per campaign; Reviewer hours per campaign; On-time campaign completion rate; Revocation follow-through rate (approved revocations actually executed); Stale/unused privileged entitlements outstanding
required_controls: Human sign-off required on every keep/revoke decision; Segregation of duties between reviewer, system owner, and revocation executor; Tamper-evident audit trail of decisions, timestamps, and reviewers; Access controls limiting who can see entitlement data by operating company; Recommendation logic documented and reviewable by audit
client_stakeholders: Chief Information Security Officer; Head of Internal Audit; IT Security / Identity & Access Management lead; Operating-company system owners; Business manager-reviewers
what_good_looks_like: Campaigns close on time with every decision human-signed and context-rich, revocations demonstrably execute, and audit pulls a complete evidence pack in minutes instead of chasing spreadsheets for weeks.
biggest_risks_traps: Copilot recommendations quietly become the decision (rubber-stamping just moves upstream) unless override behavior is monitored; Revocation routing that stops at 'requested' but never confirms execution leaves real access risk open; Entitlement data quality is worse than assumed, undermining recommendation trust; Over-automation pressure from stakeholders wanting to auto-revoke before controls are proven
gaps_in_current_moves_model: Model has no first-class notion of a recurring compliance campaign with a completion SLA versus a one-time deliverable; No native concept of 'requested vs. executed vs. verified' state for a downstream remediation action; Evidence-integrity/tamper-evidence requirements aren't an explicit building-block attribute

business_outcome: Ensure that every employee and contractor across Lakeshore's operating companies attests to required corporate policies on time, with clean, defensible proof — reducing manual chasing by compliance staff and eliminating gaps that surface as audit findings.
current_state_work_problem: Corporate compliance tracks policy attestations (code of conduct, security policy, data handling, conflict-of-interest) in spreadsheets and disconnected tools per operating company. Distribution lists are stale, reminders are sent by hand, completion status is reconciled manually, and when audit or a regulator asks 'who attested to what version, when,' the team scrambles to reassemble evidence across systems and time periods.
phase_one_solution_approach: An intelligence and tracking layer that consolidates who-owes-what across operating companies, drafts targeted reminders for compliance staff to review and send, and flags at-risk populations — with a knowledge copilot that answers employee questions about the policy in plain language. Attestations and their exact policy version are captured as clean, timestamped evidence. Compliance owns campaign launch and escalation decisions.
building_blocks: Knowledge/retrieval copilot; Workflow automation; Analytics/intelligence layer; Controls/governance/risk; Value tracking/operating cadence
building_blocks_not_yet: Human-in-the-loop agent: Attestation is inherently the employee's own act; there's no delegated agent making decisions on their behalf, so a HITL agent block adds little at P1.; AI-assisted decision support: Attestation is largely a completeness-and-coverage problem, not a judgment call; decision-support is deferred until exception-handling patterns justify it.; System/platform implementation: Standing up a new attestation platform is heavier than needed at P1; the first move rides on existing HR/identity rosters and distribution mechanisms.
required_p2_evidence: Full list of required policies, current versions, and owning functions; Current attestation rosters and how population is derived per operating company; Last cycle's completion rates, overdue counts, and time-to-complete; Audit/regulatory findings tied to attestation gaps or version ambiguity; Current reminder/escalation process and who owns it
p2_current_state_focus: Establish the true required population per policy, quantify manual chasing effort and completion gaps, and expose where version-tracking and evidence are ambiguous.
p3_solution_approach_focus: Design the consolidated tracking view, the reminder/escalation flow with human launch control, the plain-language policy copilot, and the version-anchored evidence capture.
p4_roadmap_value_focus: Quantify compliance-staff hours saved and completion-rate lift; sequence rollout by policy and by operating company; build the case on audit-defensibility and coverage.
p5_execution_focus: Run attestation cycles on cadence, monitor completion and at-risk populations, escalate exceptions to compliance owners, and produce clean evidence packs on demand.
tower_metrics: On-time attestation completion rate; Compliance-staff hours per cycle; Average time-to-complete per attestation; Coverage gap (required population not yet attested); Evidence-pack retrieval time for audit requests
required_controls: Attestation bound to the exact policy version presented; Population derivation traceable to an authoritative roster source; Immutable timestamped record of each attestation; Human control over campaign launch and escalation; Access controls on who can view attestation status by operating company
client_stakeholders: Chief Compliance Officer; Corporate policy owners (Legal, Security, HR); Head of Internal Audit; HR / people-data owners per operating company; Operating-company compliance liaisons
what_good_looks_like: Every required person attests on time to the correct policy version, compliance sees live coverage without spreadsheets, and audit evidence is one click with no reconciliation.
biggest_risks_traps: Population accuracy depends on HR/identity data that is often stale, so 'complete' can be false; Version drift — attesting to the wrong or outdated policy version quietly invalidates the evidence; Reminder fatigue if automation over-sends without human tuning; Coverage across many operating companies with different rosters is harder than a single-tenant demo suggests
gaps_in_current_moves_model: No native binding of an attestation record to a specific document version as first-class evidence; Population/roster authoritativeness isn't modeled as a prerequisite the move must validate; Recurring-cycle cadence with completion SLA still lives awkwardly in a deliverable-centric model

business_outcome: Speed up how corporate shared services collects, chases, and validates security and compliance evidence from Lakeshore's third parties (audits, certifications, insurance, questionnaires) so vendor risk reviews finish faster and no operating company onboards a vendor on stale or missing evidence.
current_state_work_problem: Third-party risk analysts email vendors for the same documents repeatedly, track responses in spreadsheets, manually read PDFs to find expiry dates and control coverage, and struggle to keep a current picture across hundreds of vendors shared by multiple operating companies. Evidence expires unnoticed, reviews stall waiting on documents, and the audit trail of what was collected and assessed is fragmented.
phase_one_solution_approach: A knowledge/retrieval copilot that reads submitted vendor evidence and surfaces key facts (certification scope, expiry, exceptions) for an analyst to verify, combined with automated outreach and follow-up to collect and refresh documents. Analysts make every risk determination; the intelligence layer keeps a live view of coverage and expiry, and all collected evidence and assessments form an auditable record.
building_blocks: Knowledge/retrieval copilot; Workflow automation; Human-in-the-loop agent; Analytics/intelligence layer; Controls/governance/risk
building_blocks_not_yet: AI-assisted decision support: Extracting and summarizing evidence comes first; scoring or recommending an overall vendor-risk rating is deferred until extraction accuracy is proven and analysts trust the inputs.; System/platform implementation: Replacing the third-party risk management platform is out of scope for P1; the move augments existing intake and tracking rather than re-platforming.; Data readiness/remediation: Historical vendor-evidence backfill is valuable but sequenced after the live collection flow proves out, to avoid boiling the ocean.
required_p2_evidence: Current vendor inventory shared across operating companies with risk tiers; Standard evidence checklist by vendor type/tier; Sample of submitted vendor documents (audits, certifications, questionnaires); Current review cycle times and backlog/aging of open reviews; Expiry-tracking approach and count of expired/unknown-status evidence
p2_current_state_focus: Quantify analyst effort per vendor, review backlog and aging, and how much evidence is expired or of unknown status; map the collection and validation workflow.
p3_solution_approach_focus: Design evidence extraction with analyst verification, automated collection/refresh outreach, the live coverage-and-expiry view, and the audit record — being explicit that the human owns every risk call.
p4_roadmap_value_focus: Quantify review cycle-time reduction, analyst capacity freed, and reduction in expired/missing evidence; sequence by vendor tier; build the case on faster onboarding and lower third-party exposure.
p5_execution_focus: Run continuous collection and refresh, monitor coverage/expiry live, escalate stalled or high-risk vendors, and maintain the audit-ready evidence record.
tower_metrics: Vendor review cycle time; Analyst hours per vendor review; Share of vendors with current (non-expired) required evidence; Open-review backlog and aging; Extraction accuracy vs. analyst correction rate
required_controls: Human verification of every extracted fact used in a risk decision; Human ownership of all vendor-risk determinations; Provenance retained linking each fact to the source document; Access controls segregating vendor data by operating company where required; Retention and integrity controls on collected evidence
client_stakeholders: Head of Third-Party / Vendor Risk; Chief Information Security Officer; Procurement / Vendor Management leads; Legal / Privacy; Operating-company business sponsors of key vendors
what_good_looks_like: Analysts spend their time judging risk, not chasing PDFs; coverage and expiry are live across all operating companies; reviews close faster; and every determination is backed by verifiable, source-linked evidence.
biggest_risks_traps: Extraction errors silently propagate into risk decisions if analyst verification is skipped under time pressure; Vendors are slow or non-responsive regardless of automation, so cycle-time gains cap out on external behavior; Shared vendors across operating companies create data-segregation and ownership ambiguity; Treating extracted summaries as authoritative rather than as analyst-assist erodes defensibility
gaps_in_current_moves_model: No first-class model of external-party document collection with expiry/refresh lifecycle; Source-provenance-per-fact isn't an explicit, auditable attribute in the current model; Cross-operating-company shared entities (one vendor, many owners) aren't cleanly represented

business_outcome: Help corporate risk and control teams triage the flood of control exceptions and policy deviations across operating companies faster and more consistently, so genuine risks get to the right owner and decision quickly and low-risk noise doesn't clog the queue — without ever auto-approving an exception.
current_state_work_problem: Control exceptions and risk-acceptance requests arrive through inconsistent channels, are described in varying quality, and land in a shared queue. Analysts manually read each one, hunt for related policy and prior similar cases, guess at severity and routing, and often let low-risk items pile up while high-risk ones wait. Consistency across reviewers is poor and the rationale for how each exception was handled is inconsistently recorded.
phase_one_solution_approach: A copilot that, for each incoming exception, retrieves the relevant policy and similar prior cases, drafts a proposed severity and routing with rationale, and prepares the packet — while a human analyst confirms severity, routing, and any approval. Exceptions are never auto-approved; the copilot only organizes, contextualizes, and recommends. Every triage decision and its rationale are recorded as auditable evidence.
building_blocks: Knowledge/retrieval copilot; AI-assisted decision support; Human-in-the-loop agent; Controls/governance/risk; Value tracking/operating cadence
building_blocks_not_yet: Workflow automation: Auto-routing and especially any auto-disposition of exceptions is deferred; at P1 the human confirms severity and routing so no exception is closed or accepted without judgment.; System/platform implementation: Replacing the GRC/exception system is out of scope; the move augments the existing intake and queue rather than re-platforming.; Analytics/intelligence layer: Portfolio-level exception analytics is valuable but sequenced after triage quality is proven; P1 focuses on per-case triage, not trend dashboards.
required_p2_evidence: Current exception/risk-acceptance intake channels and volumes; Sample of past exceptions with how they were triaged and dispositioned; Severity and routing criteria / policy mapping in use today; Cycle time and backlog/aging of the exception queue; Audit findings on exception-handling consistency or documentation
p2_current_state_focus: Quantify exception volume, triage time, backlog aging, and reviewer-to-reviewer inconsistency; map intake channels and current severity/routing logic.
p3_solution_approach_focus: Design retrieval of policy and prior cases, the recommended-severity/routing logic with rationale, the human confirmation step, and the decision-rationale evidence trail — explicit that no exception is auto-approved.
p4_roadmap_value_focus: Quantify triage-time reduction, backlog reduction, and consistency improvement; sequence by exception type and operating company; build the case on faster risk response and defensible, consistent handling.
p5_execution_focus: Run live triage on cadence, monitor triage time and analyst override rate, watch for high-severity items aging, and report consistency and audit-readiness to control owners.
tower_metrics: Average exception triage time; Exception queue backlog and aging; High-severity exception time-to-owner; Analyst override rate on recommended severity/routing; Share of exceptions with complete recorded rationale
required_controls: No auto-approval or auto-acceptance of any exception; Human confirmation of severity, routing, and disposition; Recorded rationale for every triage decision; Segregation of duties between triage, approval, and risk acceptance; Recommendation logic documented and auditable
client_stakeholders: Chief Risk Officer; Head of Internal Controls / GRC; Chief Information Security Officer; Head of Internal Audit; Operating-company control owners
what_good_looks_like: High-risk exceptions reach the right owner within hours with full context, low-risk noise is organized not ignored, triage is consistent across reviewers, and every disposition has a recorded, defensible rationale — with humans owning every accept/reject.
biggest_risks_traps: Recommended severity becomes de-facto decision, letting a mis-scored high risk slip through unless overrides are monitored; Inconsistent, low-quality intake descriptions cap recommendation accuracy; Pressure to auto-dispose 'obvious' low-risk items erodes the no-auto-approval line; Similar-case retrieval surfaces bad precedents that get copied forward
gaps_in_current_moves_model: No first-class 'triage queue with SLA-by-severity' concept distinct from a one-time deliverable; Human-override capture and monitoring isn't an explicit, measurable model attribute; Prior-case precedent quality/governance isn't modeled, risking bad-precedent propagation

use_case: Regulatory change monitoring and impact routing
business_outcome: Give corporate compliance a reliable early-warning and routing capability for regulatory and standards changes that affect Lakeshore's operating companies, so relevant changes reach the right control owner with a plain-language impact summary — reducing missed obligations and late, reactive scrambles.
current_state_work_problem: Compliance staff manually monitor a patchwork of regulators and standards bodies relevant to Lakeshore's varied industrial businesses, read dense updates, guess which operating companies and controls are affected, and forward things ad hoc. Changes are missed or noticed late, impact assessment is inconsistent, and there's no clean record showing the company saw a change and acted on it — a gap auditors and regulators probe.
phase_one_solution_approach: A knowledge/retrieval copilot that ingests regulatory and standards updates, summarizes each in plain language, and proposes which operating companies, policies, and control owners are potentially affected — for a compliance analyst to confirm and route. The analyst owns every relevance and impact judgment; the copilot triages and drafts. Each change, its assessment, and its routing form an auditable trail of awareness and response.
building_blocks: Knowledge/retrieval copilot; AI-assisted decision support; Human-in-the-loop agent; Controls/governance/risk; Value tracking/operating cadence
building_blocks_not_yet: Workflow automation: Auto-creating obligations or control changes from a detected update is deferred; a compliance human must confirm relevance and impact before anything is routed as an action at P1.; Analytics/intelligence layer: A regulatory-change portfolio dashboard is a fast-follow; P1 focuses on reliable detection, summarization, and routing of individual changes.; System/platform implementation: Standing up a full regulatory-change-management platform is heavier than needed; the first move augments existing monitoring and routing with better triage and evidence.
required_p2_evidence: List of regulators, standards, and obligation domains relevant per operating company; Current monitoring sources and how updates are found today; Mapping (even partial) of obligations to policies and control owners; Examples of recent changes and how they were assessed and routed; Any audit/regulatory findings on missed or late regulatory responses
p2_current_state_focus: Map the regulatory landscape across operating companies, quantify monitoring effort and known misses/late responses, and expose where obligation-to-owner mapping is missing.
p3_solution_approach_focus: Design source ingestion and plain-language summarization, the proposed-impact/owner routing with analyst confirmation, and the awareness-and-response evidence trail — explicit that relevance and impact are human-judged.
p4_roadmap_value_focus: Quantify monitoring hours saved, reduction in missed/late responses, and faster time-to-owner; sequence by regulatory domain and operating company; build the case on reduced regulatory exposure and demonstrable diligence.
p5_execution_focus: Run continuous monitoring, route confirmed changes to owners on cadence, track time-to-owner and closure of required responses, and maintain the auditable awareness trail.
tower_metrics: Time from regulatory change to owner notification; Compliance monitoring hours per period; Coverage of relevant sources actively monitored; Missed/late-response incidents; Analyst correction rate on proposed impact/routing
required_controls: Human confirmation of relevance, impact, and routing before action; Source provenance retained for every change summarized; Auditable record that a change was seen, assessed, and routed; Documented, reviewable impact-proposal logic; Access controls on obligation and control-owner data by operating company
client_stakeholders: Chief Compliance Officer; Chief Risk Officer; Legal / Regulatory Affairs; Operating-company compliance liaisons; Head of Internal Audit
what_good_looks_like: Relevant regulatory changes are caught early, summarized in plain English, and land with the right control owner within a defined window — with a clean, auditable record that Lakeshore saw each change and acted, and humans owning every impact call.
biggest_risks_traps: False confidence — missed sources create blind spots the copilot won't flag because it never saw them; Over-summarization loses a nuance that changes the obligation, so analyst review of source is essential; Obligation-to-owner mapping is often incomplete, so routing quality is capped by that groundwork; Pressure to treat summaries as authoritative interpretation rather than analyst-assist creates legal risk
gaps_in_current_moves_model: No first-class model of continuous external-signal monitoring with coverage/completeness as a tracked attribute; Obligation-to-control-to-owner mapping as a maintained reference isn't represented; 'Demonstrable diligence' (proof the org saw and responded) isn't an explicit evidence pattern in the model
